headline: Thursday's very powerful storm is winding down to scattered showers this evening, followed by a cool, dry Friday through Sunday afternoon and a dry, warmer Thanksgiving.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: The storm that moved through Thursday dropped extremely heavy rain, peaking at 2.26 inches in one hour over Mulholland Drive above Encino, a rate expected only about once in 100 years. Scattered showers around Glendale and the rest of the area continue into this evening, but no further significant impacts are expected. LA County has a 20% chance of a thunderstorm until about 4 PM, and a Wind Advisory runs until 4 PM this afternoon.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Friday through Sunday afternoon will be dry but cool, with highs mainly in the 60s, around 5 degrees below normal. Nights will be chilly, especially inland, where some spots could drop below freezing, most likely in the Antelope Valley and parts of interior San Luis Obispo County. Light northeast (offshore, land-to-sea) winds develop this weekend, likely topping out at 20–30 mph. A very weak system Sunday night into Monday morning brings at most about a quarter inch of rain to the Central Coast and a tenth of an inch or less farther south, including LA County.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: The rest of Monday and Tuesday will be dry with a slow warming trend. Another weak system reaches California Wednesday, but computer models disagree on whether it brings any rain here; if it does it probably won't be much, though a small share of model runs show around a half inch. Thanksgiving Day is expected to be dry, with offshore winds pushing temperatures into the 70s.

coast: High Surf Advisories cover all beaches into Friday (ending between 3 AM and 9 PM Friday depending on the beach), with large surf creating very dangerous rip currents and hazardous conditions near jetties; large breaking waves may hit Morro Bay Harbor, and to a lesser extent Ventura Harbor, through tonight. Ocean conditions stay dangerous through tonight from gusty winds and large, still-building seas, with Small Craft Advisories ending between 3 AM and 9 PM Friday; conditions improve Friday and turn fairly mild Saturday, and a weak front Sunday into Monday should have minimal impact. A stronger cold front could bring wind and rain to the coastal waters Tuesday night into Wednesday, with large seas returning mid to late next week. Extremely high, likely record-breaking tides arrive Thanksgiving week (peaking Tuesday through Thanksgiving Day), and combined with more swells they will likely cause at least widespread moderate coastal flooding on all coasts, with significant flooding possible if a larger swell lines up with the highest tides.
watch_for: Whether Wednesday's weak system brings any rain to LA County before a dry Thanksgiving.
Sub-freezing overnight lows this weekend in the Antelope Valley and interior San Luis Obispo County.
Record-high tides Tuesday through Thanksgiving combined with new swells, raising the risk of widespread coastal flooding.
confidence: Forecasters are confident the storm's impacts are ending and in dry weather Friday through Sunday afternoon, but less sure about rain chances with Wednesday's system because computer models are mixed.
